# 1 Clement Chapter 63 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 63

---

## Council Notes

**On "submit the neck" / "bow the neck in submission" (v.1):** EMET: "submit the neck." LOGOS: "bow the neck in submission." PNEUMA: "bow our necks in submission." The Greek *upotassein ton trachēlon* is a submission idiom from ancient rhetoric and military practice (the defeated bow the neck before the conqueror). "Bow the neck in submission" (LOGOS) best preserves the idiom. Clement immediately glosses it: "that is, to practice obedience."

**On "futile sedition" / "futile rebellion" (v.1):** All agents agree. The *mataian stasin* (vain/futile faction) echoes the letter's opening complaint. "Futile sedition" (EMET/LOGOS) is retained — *stasis* as "sedition" throughout.

**On "root out" / "uproot" (v.2):** EMET: "root out." LOGOS: "uproot." PNEUMA: "tear out by the root." The Greek *ekripsantes* means "having uprooted/torn out." "Uproot" (LOGOS) is clean and literal.

**On the letter-bearers (v.3):** Clement names them in Ch.65. Here he introduces them. "Faithful and prudent men" — the Greek *pistous kai sōphronas* = faithful and sensible/prudent. All agents agree.

**On "written through the Holy Spirit" (v.2):** This is a significant claim — Clement regards his letter as written through the Holy Spirit. All agents preserve this. It elevates the letter toward quasi-canonical status.

---

**63:1** Therefore it is right that we should be attentive to so many and such great examples, and bow the neck in submission — that is, practice obedience — so that, laying aside the futile sedition, we may attain without any reproach the goal set before us in truth.

**63:2** For you will give us joy and gladness if you are obedient to what we have written through the Holy Spirit and uproot the unlawful passion of your jealousy, in accordance with the entreaty for peace and harmony which we have penned in this letter.

**63:3** We have also sent to you faithful and prudent men who from youth to old age have lived virtuously among us, and they shall be witnesses between you and us.

**63:4** This we have done so that you may know that our entire concern has been and is that you should quickly attain peace.

---

*— SOPHIA*
